title: Dark bands: overhangs and objects fixed, the dig left as agreed
question: Panels 1 and 2 are what you signed off — do the overhang and the suspended slab now read as outdoors to you, and is the pit in panel 3 acceptable to leave black for now?
context_md:
The per-cell genesis map landed: one bit per cell, "was this enclosed when the world was made", seeded by a flood fill at generation. `dead-ends.md` §977's *store more history, never infer* — no width threshold anywhere, and a dug shaft still stays a tunnel at any width.

**Before images are on the previous card** (`20260822T235306955Z-ac8c28`), same scenes, same crops.

Measured: rescues 149/156, 406/408, 192/197 of the false-cave cells on seeds 1-3. The remainder were rock at genesis and are air now — dark by the same rule as a dug shaft. Costs **+0.3 to +0.7 ms on a ~11.5 ms full redraw**, measured interleaved against a worktree at the parent commit because the machine drifted upward during the run.

**One residual I did not fix, and it is visible in panel 2:** the rock *under* the slab is still over-darkened — a faint band across the pool floor. The decision is now per cell but the *depth* still comes from the per-column datum, and the notch-clipping only clips dips, not spikes. The honest fix is a depth measured from the nearest outdoors cell, which is the same distance transform the pit case needs, so I left it to go with that work rather than bolting it on.

On your "better solution" for the pit — prior art written up in `Reports/prior-art-underground-lighting.md`. Terraria does exactly what you described wanting: a per-tile **wall** layer decides whether sky light can enter (mining does not remove the wall, so your tunnel stays dark), and then light *propagates* at 0.91 per air tile and 0.56 per solid tile. That second half is what makes a wide pit bright at the top and dark at the bottom with no threshold. Noita does the opposite — no classification at all, everything dark until lit, via a coarse 32x32 fog of war that they had to **blur** because as plain tiles it read as a grid (which is our own open bug 0c, exactly). We already compute the Beer-Lambert channel Terraria's half needs, in `field.rs`, and nothing draws it.

items.label: 1 — natural cliff brow (real world, seed 1)
items.caption: Second tile. The hard-edged darker patch of sky off the lip is gone.

items.label: 2 — slab suspended at genesis (scene=rockdrop, frame 1)
items.caption: The band through the air and through the pond is gone. The faint darkening still on the pool floor at the bottom is the residual described above.

items.label: 3 — the open-cast pit, left black on purpose
items.caption: 64 wide, 40 deep, nothing overhead. Unchanged: those cells were rock at genesis.
